items.name: reflex-dev/xy
items.brief: Fourth day on the list and the only entry today confirmed by three unrelated collectors — npm downloads, GitHub stars and HackerNews. Downloads are up 41% week over week against 4.4% star growth, and 65 open issues on 1,296 stars is a high ratio: people are running it in anger rather than admiring it. The watcher count sits at 3, which is the one discordant note — almost nobody has committed to following the project despite using it.

items.name: mokshablr/gander
items.brief: 207 HackerNews points and 75 comments against 287 stars and 4 forks. Attention running well ahead of adoption: a lot of people read about it, very few took it home. Stars grew 7.4% and forks 9.1% overnight, so the gap is closing slowly rather than not at all. It has already left the front page, which makes the next two days the test.

items.name: createcentercv.org
items.brief: Movement across three independent readings — Majestic, OpenPageRank and Tranco — but all of it small: rank up 5%, subnets up 1.4%. The value here is the agreement rather than the size. Three unrelated crawls noticing the same modest climb is a different claim from one crawl noticing a big one.

items.name: gogadgetz.nl
items.brief: Rank improved 3.9% while referring IPs FELL 42% and subnets rose 3.7%. Losing links from one network while gaining them from others usually means a single large linking site dropped it. The rank held anyway, which is mildly reassuring, but the two numbers point in opposite directions and neither is large.

items.name: sttatiana-omsk.ru
items.brief: Referring IPs up 294% and referring subnets up 217% in a single day. That is not organic link acquisition — a genuine site does not triple its backlink footprint overnight, and the shape is what a purchased link blast looks like. Included deliberately rather than hidden: this is the kind of entry the noise gate should be catching and currently is not, because the link-network rule looks for clusters of domains acting together and this is one domain acting alone.

items.name: walkntalkrepair.co.uk
items.brief: Referring IPs up 84% against subnets up 17% — five times as many new links as new networks. That ratio means a handful of sites linked repeatedly rather than many sites linking once, which is weaker evidence than the raw percentage suggests. A UK repair business, probably real, probably having a good week rather than breaking out.

items.name: wikif1.org
items.brief: An F1 wiki with 1.5% rank movement and 1% subnet growth. Genuinely marginal — it clears the corroboration bar because two independent sources both registered the same small climb. Listed for honesty about what today's threshold admits.

items.name: playscrabble.com
items.brief: Same shape as createcentercv: three sources, all agreeing, none dramatic. Rank up 5.4% with subnets up 2%. A long-established word-game site — this is what steady looks like, and it is here to show that the corroboration rule fires on ordinary movement too, not only on spikes.

items.name: payfix.nl
items.brief: Rank improved 66% with referring IPs and subnets both up around 20%, which is a far more plausible ratio than the Russian entry above — links arriving from many distinct networks rather than one. A Dutch payments-adjacent site with real authority movement. Worth a look, though the Tranco rank slipped slightly, so traffic has not followed the links yet.

items.name: mondomedia.com
items.brief: Referring IPs up 29% and subnets up 28% — one new link per network, which is the healthy shape. Rank change of 35% on an established media domain. The near-identical IP and subnet growth is what genuine link acquisition looks like and is the clearest contrast on this page with the Omsk entry.

items.name: semenovpolk.ru
items.brief: Tranco traffic rank improved 22% with no backlink movement at all. Traffic without links is either a referral spike or a news mention, and neither is visible from here. A Russian military-history site; the movement is real but unexplained by anything else we measure.

items.name: luanascowcroft.co.nz
items.brief: Tranco rank up 16%, nothing else moving. A New Zealand personal or small-business site. This is the weakest kind of entry on the page: one source showing movement, a second merely confirming the domain exists and has authority. Two sources technically, one signal actually.
